name_translation: The Yoga of the Three Modes of Material Nature

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
परं भूयः प्रवक्ष्यामि ज्ञानानां ज्ञानमुत्तमम् |
यज्ज्ञात्वा मुनयः सर्वे परां सिद्धिमितो गताः || १ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
परं भूयः प्रवक्ष्यामि ज्ञानानां ज्ञानमुत्तमम् |
यज्ज्ञात्वा मुनयः सर्वे परां सिद्धिमितो गताः || १ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
paraṃ bhūyaḥ pravakṣyāmi jñānānāṃ jñānamuttamam |
yajjñātvā munayaḥ sarve parāṃ siddhimito gatāḥ || 1 ||
verses.word_meanings: śrī-bhagavān uvāca—the Supreme Lord said; param—supreme/transcendental; bhūyaḥ—again; pravakṣyāmi—I shall declare; jñānānām—of all knowledge; jñānam uttamam—the supreme wisdom; yat—which; jñātvā—knowing; munayaḥ—the sages/seers; sarve—all; parām—supreme; siddhim—perfection; itaḥ—from this mortal world; gatāḥ—have attained.
verses.translation: The Supreme Lord said: I shall once again declare to you that supreme wisdom, the highest of all knowledge, by realizing which all the sages have attained the supreme perfection beyond this mortal world.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna begins the fourteenth chapter by underscoring the transcendental supremacy of this teaching. Chapter 13 analyzed the Field (matter) and the Knower (spirit); Chapter 14 dissects the internal mechanics of matter—the three modes (Gunas) of Prakriti—that bind the soul, and provides the definitive formula for transcending them to attain Brahman.
verses.purport: Sri Krishna begins the fourteenth chapter by underscoring the transcendental supremacy of this teaching. Chapter 13 analyzed the Field (matter) and the Knower (spirit); Chapter 14 dissects the internal mechanics of matter—the three modes (Gunas) of Prakriti—that bind the soul, and provides the definitive formula for transcending them to attain Brahman.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
इदं ज्ञानमुपाश्रित्य मम साधर्म्यमागताः |
सर्गेऽपि नोपजायन्ते प्रलये न व्यथन्ति च || २ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
इदं ज्ञानमुपाश्रित्य मम साधर्म्यमागताः |
सर्गेऽपि नोपजायन्ते प्रलये न व्यथन्ति च || २ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
idaṃ jñānamupāśritya mama sādharmyamāgatāḥ |
sarge'pi nopajāyante pralaye na vyathanti ca || 2 ||
verses.word_meanings: idam—this; jñānam—wisdom; upāśritya—taking refuge in; mama—My; sādharmyam—divine nature / unity of qualities; āgatāḥ—having attained; sarge api—even at the time of cosmic creation; na upajāyante—they are not born; pralaye—at the time of cosmic dissolution; na—not; vyathanti—are disturbed/grieved; ca—and.
verses.translation: Having taken refuge in this wisdom and attained unity with My divine nature (Sadharmya), they are not born even at the time of cosmic creation, nor are they disturbed at the time of universal dissolution.
verses.meaning: Sadharmya denotes attaining the divine spiritual nature of God—immortality, infinite consciousness, and uninterrupted bliss. Liberated souls who realize this wisdom transcend the cosmic cycles of creation (Srishti) and dissolution (Pralaya), abiding eternally in the Supreme.
verses.purport: Sadharmya denotes attaining the divine spiritual nature of God—immortality, infinite consciousness, and uninterrupted bliss. Liberated souls who realize this wisdom transcend the cosmic cycles of creation (Srishti) and dissolution (Pralaya), abiding eternally in the Supreme.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मम योनिर्महद्ब्रह्म तस्मिन्गर्भं दधाम्यहम् |
सम्भवः सर्वभूतानां ततो भवति भारत || ३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मम योनिर्महद्ब्रह्म तस्मिन्गर्भं दधाम्यहम् |
सम्भवः सर्वभूतानां ततो भवति भारत || ३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
mama yonirmahadbrahma tasmingarbhaṃ dadhāmyaham |
sambhavaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ tato bhavati bhārata || 3 ||
verses.word_meanings: mama—My; yoniḥ—womb / source of birth; mahat brahma—the great unmanifest cosmic nature (Mahat-Tattva / Prakriti); tasmin—in that; garbham—the seed/embryo of life; dadhāmi—impregnate / cast; aham—I; sambhavaḥ—the manifestation/origin; sarva-bhūtānām—of all living beings; tataḥ—from that; bhavati—occurs; bhārata—O descendant of Bharata (Arjuna).
verses.translation: My womb is the great unmanifest primordial nature (Mahad-Brahma); into that I plant the seed of consciousness. From that impregnation, O Bharata, arises the generation of all living beings.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna explains the cosmic genesis: Primordial matter (Prakriti, here called Mahad-Brahma) is the cosmic womb. The Supreme Lord impregnates this inert matter with the spark of individual conscious souls (Jivas), generating the multifaceted tapestry of living beings across the universe.
verses.purport: Sri Krishna explains the cosmic genesis: Primordial matter (Prakriti, here called Mahad-Brahma) is the cosmic womb. The Supreme Lord impregnates this inert matter with the spark of individual conscious souls (Jivas), generating the multifaceted tapestry of living beings across the universe.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सर्वयोनिषु कौन्तेय मूर्तयः सम्भवन्ति याः |
तासां ब्रह्म महद्योनिरहं बीजप्रदः पिता || ४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सर्वयोनिषु कौन्तेय मूर्तयः सम्भवन्ति याः |
तासां ब्रह्म महद्योनिरहं बीजप्रदः पिता || ४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
sarvayoniṣu kaunteya mūrtayaḥ sambhavanti yāḥ |
tāsāṃ brahma mahadyonirahaṃ bījapradaḥ pitā || 4 ||
verses.word_meanings: sarva-yoniṣu—in all species of life / wombs; kaunteya—O son of Kunti (Arjuna); mūrtayaḥ—embodied forms/creatures; sambhavanti—are born/manifest; yāḥ—which; tāsām—of them; brahma mahat—the great material nature; yoniḥ—the mother/womb; aham—I (the Supreme Lord); bīja-pradaḥ—the seed-giving; pitā—father.
verses.translation: Whatever bodily forms are produced in all species of life, O Kaunteya, the great material nature is their motherly womb, and I am the seed-giving Father.
verses.meaning: This core verse establishes the universal parenthood of the cosmos: Mother Nature (Prakriti) provides the material physical elements and bodily vehicles, while Sri Krishna is the eternal Divine Father who bestows the living spark of consciousness. Thus all living entities across all species are interconnected children of the one Supreme Lord.
verses.purport: This core verse establishes the universal parenthood of the cosmos: Mother Nature (Prakriti) provides the material physical elements and bodily vehicles, while Sri Krishna is the eternal Divine Father who bestows the living spark of consciousness. Thus all living entities across all species are interconnected children of the one Supreme Lord.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सत्त्वं रजस्तम इति गुणाः प्रकृतिसम्भवाः |
निबध्नन्ति महाबाहो देहे देहिनमव्ययम् || ५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सत्त्वं रजस्तम इति गुणाः प्रकृतिसम्भवाः |
निबध्नन्ति महाबाहो देहे देहिनमव्ययम् || ५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
sattvaṃ rajastama iti guṇāḥ prakṛtisambhavāḥ |
nibadhnanti mahābāho dehe dehinamavyayam || 5 ||
verses.word_meanings: sattvam—goodness/purity; rajaḥ—passion; tamaḥ—ignorance/darkness; iti—thus; guṇāḥ—the three modes/qualities; prakṛti-sambhavāḥ—born of material nature; nibadhnanti—bind fast; mahā-bāho—O mighty-armed one (Arjuna); dehe—in the body; dehinam—the embodied soul; avyayam—the imperishable/immutable.
verses.translation: Sattva (purity), Rajas (passion), and Tamas (inertia)—these three modes born of material nature, O mighty-armed Arjuna, bind fast in the physical body the imperishable embodied soul.
verses.meaning: The word 'Guna' literally means 'rope' or 'strand'. Just as three strands are twisted into a strong rope, Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas intertwine to bind the intrinsically free and immortal Soul (Dehi) to the psychophysical body through psychological attachments and identification.
verses.purport: The word 'Guna' literally means 'rope' or 'strand'. Just as three strands are twisted into a strong rope, Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas intertwine to bind the intrinsically free and immortal Soul (Dehi) to the psychophysical body through psychological attachments and identification.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तत्र सत्त्वं निर्मलत्वात्प्रकाशकमनामयम् |
सुखसङ्गेन बध्नाति ज्ञानसङ्गेन चानघ || ६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तत्र सत्त्वं निर्मलत्वात्प्रकाशकमनामयम् |
सुखसङ्गेन बध्नाति ज्ञानसङ्गेन चानघ || ६ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
tatra sattvaṃ nirmalatvātprakāśakamanāmayam |
sukhasaṅgena badhnāti jñānasaṅgena cānagha || 6 ||
verses.word_meanings: tatra—of these; sattvam—the mode of goodness/purity; nirmalatvāt—due to being pure and clear; prakāśakam—illuminating; anāmayam—free from disease/evil; sukha-saṅgena—by attachment to happiness; badhnāti—binds; jñāna-saṅgena—by attachment to knowledge; ca—and; anagha—O sinless one (Arjuna).
verses.translation: Of these, Sattva (goodness), on account of its purity, is illuminating and free from all afflictions; it binds the soul, O sinless one, through attachment to happiness and attachment to intellectual knowledge.
verses.meaning: Sattva is like a spotless crystal pane: it transmits divine light, cultivates peace, virtue, and intellectual clarity. However, it still creates subtle spiritual bondage through pride of knowledge ('I am wise') and longing for serenity ('I must possess uninterrupted peace'). Even a golden chain is still a chain.
verses.purport: Sattva is like a spotless crystal pane: it transmits divine light, cultivates peace, virtue, and intellectual clarity. However, it still creates subtle spiritual bondage through pride of knowledge ('I am wise') and longing for serenity ('I must possess uninterrupted peace'). Even a golden chain is still a chain.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
रजो रागात्मकं विद्धि तृष्णासङ्गसमुद्भवम् |
तन्निबध्नाति कौन्तेय कर्मसङ्गेन देहिनम् || ७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
रजो रागात्मकं विद्धि तृष्णासङ्गसमुद्भवम् |
तन्निबध्नाति कौन्तेय कर्मसङ्गेन देहिनम् || ७ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
rajo rāgātmakaṃ viddhi tṛṣṇāsaṅgasamudbhavam |
tannibadhnāti kaunteya karmasaṅgena dehinam || 7 ||
verses.word_meanings: rajaḥ—the mode of passion; rāga-ātmakam—consisting of intense longing/passion; viddhi—know; tṛṣṇā-saṅga-samudbhavam—arising from insatiable thirst and attachment; tat—that; nibadhnāti—binds; kaunteya—O son of Kunti (Arjuna); karma-saṅgena—by attachment to fruitive action; dehinam—the embodied soul.
verses.translation: Know Rajas (passion) to be of the nature of intense attraction, arising from insatiable thirst and worldly attachment. It binds the embodied soul fast, O Kaunteya, by attachment to fruitive actions and results.
verses.meaning: Rajas is characterized by dynamic restlessness, ambition, and emotional craving (Raga). It drives beings into ceaseless striving for wealth, prestige, and sensory gratification, binding the soul through relentless anxiety over the fruits of labor.
verses.purport: Rajas is characterized by dynamic restlessness, ambition, and emotional craving (Raga). It drives beings into ceaseless striving for wealth, prestige, and sensory gratification, binding the soul through relentless anxiety over the fruits of labor.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तमस्त्वज्ञानजं विद्धि मोहनं सर्वदेहिनाम् |
प्रमादालस्यनिद्राभिस्तन्निबध्नाति भारत || ८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तमस्त्वज्ञानजं विद्धि मोहनं सर्वदेहिनाम् |
प्रमादालस्यनिद्राभिस्तन्निबध्नाति भारत || ८ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
tamastvajñānajaṃ viddhi mohanaṃ sarvadehinām |
pramādālasyanidrābhistannibadhnāti bhārata || 8 ||
verses.word_meanings: tamaḥ—the mode of ignorance/darkness; tu—but; ajñāna-jam—born of ignorance/nescience; viddhi—know; mohanam—deluding/bewildering; sarva-dehinām—of all embodied beings; pramāda-ālasya-nidrābhiḥ—by negligence, indolence, and excessive sleep; tat—that; nibadhnāti—binds; bhārata—O descendant of Bharata (Arjuna).
verses.translation: Know Tamas (ignorance/darkness), however, to be born of nescience, the deluder of all embodied beings. It binds the soul, O Bharata, by negligence (Pramada), indolence (Alasya), and excessive sleep (Nidra).
verses.meaning: Tamas veils reality completely like thick dark clouds. It generates apathy, confusion, procrastination, lethargy, and intoxication, pulling consciousness into heedlessness and delusion.
verses.purport: Tamas veils reality completely like thick dark clouds. It generates apathy, confusion, procrastination, lethargy, and intoxication, pulling consciousness into heedlessness and delusion.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सत्त्वं सुखे सञ्जयति रजः कर्मणि भारत |
ज्ञानमावृत्य तु तमः प्रमादे सञ्जयत्युत || ९ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सत्त्वं सुखे सञ्जयति रजः कर्मणि भारत |
ज्ञानमावृत्य तु तमः प्रमादे सञ्जयत्युत || ९ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
sattvaṃ sukhe sañjayati rajaḥ karmaṇi bhārata |
jñānamāvṛtya tu tamaḥ pramāde sañjayatyuta || 9 ||
verses.word_meanings: sattvam—Sattva; sukhe—in happiness; sañjayati—attaches/binds; rajaḥ—Rajas; karmaṇi—in action; bhārata—O descendant of Bharata; jñānam—knowledge/wisdom; āvṛtya—veiling/covering; tu—indeed; tamaḥ—Tamas; pramāde—in negligence/folly; sañjayati—binds; uta—certainly.
verses.translation: Sattva attaches one to joy, Rajas attaches one to action, O Bharata, whereas Tamas, veiling true wisdom, binds one to heedlessness and error.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna encapsulates the core binding power of the three modes: Sattva binds to inner harmony and bliss; Rajas binds to feverish labor and ambition; Tamas smothers the light of discernment and binds to delusion and carelessness.
verses.purport: Sri Krishna encapsulates the core binding power of the three modes: Sattva binds to inner harmony and bliss; Rajas binds to feverish labor and ambition; Tamas smothers the light of discernment and binds to delusion and carelessness.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
रजस्तमश्चाभिभूय सत्त्वं भवति भारत |
रजः सत्त्वं तमश्चैव तमः सत्त्वं रजस्तथा || १० ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
रजस्तमश्चाभिभूय सत्त्वं भवति भारत |
रजः सत्त्वं तमश्चैव तमः सत्त्वं रजस्तथा || १० ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
rajastamaścābhibhūya sattvaṃ bhavati bhārata |
rajaḥ sattvaṃ tamaścaiva tamaḥ sattvaṃ rajastathā || 10 ||
verses.word_meanings: rajaḥ—Rajas; tamaḥ ca—and Tamas; abhibhūya—overpowering; sattvam—Sattva; bhavati—arises/prevails; bhārata—O Bharata; rajaḥ—Rajas; sattvam tamaḥ ca eva—overpowering Sattva and Tamas; tamaḥ—Tamas; sattvam rajaḥ tathā—overpowering Sattva and Rajas likewise.
verses.translation: Overpowering Rajas and Tamas, Sattva prevails, O Bharata; overcoming Sattva and Tamas, Rajas rises; and overpowering Sattva and Rajas, Tamas dominates.
verses.meaning: The three Gunas are in constant dynamic flux and rivalry within the human psyche. At any given moment, one Guna ascends by subordinating the other two. The spiritual aspirant learns to recognize these shifts and systematically cultivate Sattva while diminishing Rajas and Tamas.
verses.purport: The three Gunas are in constant dynamic flux and rivalry within the human psyche. At any given moment, one Guna ascends by subordinating the other two. The spiritual aspirant learns to recognize these shifts and systematically cultivate Sattva while diminishing Rajas and Tamas.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सर्वद्वारेषु देहेऽस्मिन्प्रकाश उपजायते |
ज्ञानं यदा तदा विद्याद्विवृद्धं सत्त्वमित्युत || ११ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सर्वद्वारेषु देहेऽस्मिन्प्रकाश उपजायते |
ज्ञानं यदा तदा विद्याद्विवृद्धं सत्त्वमित्युत || ११ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
sarvadvāreṣu dehe'sminprakāśa upajāyate |
jñānaṃ yadā tadā vidyādvivṛddhaṃ sattvamityuta || 11 ||
verses.word_meanings: sarva-dvāreṣu—in all the gates (senses); dehe asmin—in this body; prakāśaḥ—the light of illumination; upajāyate—arises/manifests; jñānam—wisdom/perception; yadā—when; tadā—then; vidyāt—one should know; vivṛddham—predominant/ascendant; sattvam—the mode of Sattva; iti uta—indeed.
verses.translation: When the illuminating light of wisdom shines through all the nine gates (senses) of this body, then one should know that Sattva is predominantly ascendant.
verses.meaning: The somatic and psychological sign of Sattva is clarity: eyes see truth, ears listen to uplifting wisdom, thoughts are tranquil, and understanding is razor-sharp.
verses.purport: The somatic and psychological sign of Sattva is clarity: eyes see truth, ears listen to uplifting wisdom, thoughts are tranquil, and understanding is razor-sharp.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
लोभः प्रवृत्तिरारम्भः कर्मणामशमः स्पृहः |
रजस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे भरतर्षभ || १२ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
लोभः प्रवृत्तिरारम्भः कर्मणामशमः स्पृहः |
रजस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे भरतर्षभ || १२ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
lobhaḥ pravṛttirārambhaḥ karmaṇāmaśamaḥ spṛhaḥ |
rajasyetāni jāyante vivṛddhe bharatarṣabha || 12 ||
verses.word_meanings: lobhaḥ—greed/covetousness; pravṛttiḥ—restless activity; ārambhaḥ karmaṇām—undertaking of self-serving projects; aśamaḥ—unrest/agitation; spṛhā—yearning/craving; rajasi—when Rajas; etāni—these; jāyante—arise; vivṛddhe—is predominant; bharata-ṛṣabha—O best of the Bharatas (Arjuna).
verses.translation: Greed, relentless activity, undertaking of self-seeking projects, restlessness, and yearning—these arise when Rajas is predominantly ascendant, O best of the Bharatas.
verses.meaning: When Rajas surges, the mind is swept by ambition, consumerist desire, feverish overwork, dissatisfaction with current possessions, and continuous longing for more.
verses.purport: When Rajas surges, the mind is swept by ambition, consumerist desire, feverish overwork, dissatisfaction with current possessions, and continuous longing for more.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अप्रकाशोऽप्रवृत्तिश्च प्रमादो मोह एव च |
तमस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे कुरुनन्दन || १३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अप्रकाशोऽप्रवृत्तिश्च प्रमादो मोह एव च |
तमस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे कुरुनन्दन || १३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
aprakāśo'pravṛttiśca pramādo moha eva ca |
tamasyetāni jāyante vivṛddhe kurunandana || 13 ||
verses.word_meanings: aprakāśaḥ—darkness/gloom; apravṛttiḥ—inertia/inactivity; ca—and; pramādaḥ—carelessness/negligence; mohaḥ—delusion/bewilderment; eva ca—and also; tamasi—when Tamas; etāni—these; jāyante—arise; vivṛddhe—is predominant; kuru-nandana—O descendant of Kuru (Arjuna).
verses.translation: Darkness, complete inertia, negligence, and delusion—these arise when Tamas is predominantly ascendant, O descendant of Kuru.
verses.meaning: When Tamas takes over, a person experiences mental fog, unmotivated sloth, inability to make decisions, procrastination, and foolish choices contrary to their own well-being.
verses.purport: When Tamas takes over, a person experiences mental fog, unmotivated sloth, inability to make decisions, procrastination, and foolish choices contrary to their own well-being.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यदा सत्त्वे प्रवृद्धे तु प्रलयं याति देहभृत् |
तदोत्तमविदां लोकानमलान्प्रतिपद्यते || १४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यदा सत्त्वे प्रवृद्धे तु प्रलयं याति देहभृत् |
तदोत्तमविदां लोकानमलान्प्रतिपद्यते || १४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yadā sattve pravṛddhe tu pralayaṃ yāti dehabhṛt |
tadottamavidāṃ lokānamalānpratipadyate || 14 ||
verses.word_meanings: yadā—when; sattve pravṛddhe—while Sattva is predominant; tu—indeed; pralayam yāti—meets death/dissolution; deha-bhṛt—the embodied soul; tadā—then; uttama-vidām—of the knowers of the highest truth; lokān—the realms/worlds; amalān—pure/stainless; pratipadyate—attains.
verses.translation: When the embodied soul meets death while Sattva is predominantly ascendant, he ascends to the spotless, pure higher realms of the knowers of the highest truth.
verses.meaning: The prevailing state of consciousness at the moment of departure determines the soul's destination. Dying with a serene, sattvic mind leads to higher celestial dimensions (Svarga and higher planetary spheres of pure light).
verses.purport: The prevailing state of consciousness at the moment of departure determines the soul's destination. Dying with a serene, sattvic mind leads to higher celestial dimensions (Svarga and higher planetary spheres of pure light).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
रजसि प्रलयं गत्वा कर्मसङ्गिषु जायते |
तथा प्रलीनस्तमसि मूढयोनिषु जायते || १५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
रजसि प्रलयं गत्वा कर्मसङ्गिषु जायते |
तथा प्रलीनस्तमसि मूढयोनिषु जायते || १५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
rajasi pralayaṃ gatvā karmasaṅgiṣu jāyate |
tathā pralīnastamasi mūḍhayoniṣu jāyate || 15 ||
verses.word_meanings: rajasi—in Rajas; pralayam gatvā—meeting death; karma-saṅgiṣu—among those attached to action (human world); jāyate—is born; tathā—likewise; pralīnaḥ—dying; tamasi—in Tamas; mūḍha-yoniṣu—in the wombs of the ignorant/animals; jāyate—is born.
verses.translation: Departing in Rajas, he is reborn among those attached to fruitive action (in the human realm); and dying in Tamas, he is reborn in the wombs of irrational species (animals and sub-human realms).
verses.meaning: Dying while burning with worldly ambitions (Rajas) brings reincarnation into active human societies driven by karma; dying steeped in stupor, addiction, or cruelty (Tamas) causes devolution into lower animalistic wombs.
verses.purport: Dying while burning with worldly ambitions (Rajas) brings reincarnation into active human societies driven by karma; dying steeped in stupor, addiction, or cruelty (Tamas) causes devolution into lower animalistic wombs.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
कर्मणः सुकृतस्याहुः सात्त्विकं निर्मलं फलम् |
रजसस्तु फलं दुःखमज्ञानं तमसः फलम् || १६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
कर्मणः सुकृतस्याहुः सात्त्विकं निर्मलं फलम् |
रजसस्तु फलं दुःखमज्ञानं तमसः फलम् || १६ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
karmaṇaḥ sukṛtasyāhuḥ sāttvikaṃ nirmalaṃ phalam |
rajasastu phalaṃ duḥkhamajñānaṃ tamasaḥ phalam || 16 ||
verses.word_meanings: karmaṇaḥ sukṛtasya—of virtuous, pure action; āhuḥ—they declare; sāttvikam—Sattvic; nirmalam—spotless/pure; phalam—the fruit; rajasaḥ tu—of Rajas indeed; phalam—fruit; duḥkham—sorrow/pain; ajñānam—ignorance; tamasaḥ—of Tamas; phalam—the fruit.
verses.translation: The fruit of virtuous action is said to be pure and Sattvic; the fruit of Rajas is pain and sorrow; and the fruit of Tamas is ignorance and darkness.
verses.meaning: Every action bears fruit identical to its underlying Guna: Sattvic actions yield inner peace and clarity; Rajasic actions yield eventual misery and disillusionment; Tamasic actions yield deepened stupor and spiritual blindness.
verses.purport: Every action bears fruit identical to its underlying Guna: Sattvic actions yield inner peace and clarity; Rajasic actions yield eventual misery and disillusionment; Tamasic actions yield deepened stupor and spiritual blindness.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सत्त्वात्सञ्जायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च |
प्रमादमोहौ तमसो भवतोऽज्ञानमेव च || १७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सत्त्वात्सञ्जायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च |
प्रमादमोहौ तमसो भवतोऽज्ञानमेव च || १७ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
sattvātsañjāyate jñānaṃ rajaso lobha eva ca |
pramādamohau tamaso bhavato'jñānameva ca || 17 ||
verses.word_meanings: sattvāt—from Sattva; sañjāyate—arises; jñānam—wisdom/knowledge; rajasaḥ—from Rajas; lobhaḥ—greed; eva ca—and also; pramāda-mohau—negligence and delusion; tamasaḥ—from Tamas; bhavataḥ—arise; ajñānam—ignorance; eva ca—and also.
verses.translation: From Sattva arises true knowledge; from Rajas arises greed; and from Tamas arise negligence, delusion, and ignorance.
verses.meaning: The Lord clearly maps the psychological harvest of each Guna: Sattva blossoms into enlightenment, Rajas degenerates into insatiable greed, and Tamas produces folly and darkness.
verses.purport: The Lord clearly maps the psychological harvest of each Guna: Sattva blossoms into enlightenment, Rajas degenerates into insatiable greed, and Tamas produces folly and darkness.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ऊर्ध्वं गच्छन्ति सत्त्वस्था मध्ये तिष्ठन्ति राजसाः |
जघन्यगुणवृत्तिस्था अधो गच्छन्ति तामसाः || १८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ऊर्ध्वं गच्छन्ति सत्त्वस्था मध्ये तिष्ठन्ति राजसाः |
जघन्यगुणवृत्तिस्था अधो गच्छन्ति तामसाः || १८ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
ūrdhvaṃ gacchanti sattvasthā madhye tiṣṭhanti rājasāḥ |
jaghanyaguṇavṛttisthā adho gacchanti tāmasāḥ || 18 ||
verses.word_meanings: ūrdhvam—upwards (to higher realms); gacchanti—go/ascend; sattva-sthāḥ—those established in Sattva; madhye—in the middle (human planes); tiṣṭhanti—abide/stay; rājasāḥ—the Rajasic; jaghanya-guṇa-vṛtti-sthāḥ—abiding in the lowest degradation of the modes; adhaḥ—downwards (to animal/hellish realms); gacchanti—sink/go; tāmasāḥ—the Tamasic.
verses.translation: Those established in Sattva ascend upwards to higher realms; the Rajasic abide in the middle (human) planes; while the Tamasic, steeped in the lowest degradations of nature, sink downwards into lower realms.
verses.meaning: This cosmic schematic illustrates the vertical trajectory of souls across the multi-tiered universe: Sattva elevates, Rajas stabilizes in the human sphere of choice, and Tamas pulls the soul downward into sub-human degradation.
verses.purport: This cosmic schematic illustrates the vertical trajectory of souls across the multi-tiered universe: Sattva elevates, Rajas stabilizes in the human sphere of choice, and Tamas pulls the soul downward into sub-human degradation.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
नान्यं गुणेभ्यः कर्तारं यदा द्रष्टानुपश्यति |
गुणेभ्यश्च परं वेत्ति मद्भावं सोऽधिगच्छति || १९ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
नान्यं गुणेभ्यः कर्तारं यदा द्रष्टानुपश्यति |
गुणेभ्यश्च परं वेत्ति मद्भावं सोऽधिगच्छति || १९ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
nānyaṃ guṇebhyaḥ kartāraṃ yadā draṣṭānupaśyati |
guṇebhyaśca paraṃ vetti madbhāvaṃ so'dhigacchati || 19 ||
verses.word_meanings: na anyam—no other; guṇebhyaḥ—than the gunas (modes); kartāram—agent/doer; yadā—when; draṣṭā—the awakened seer; anupaśyati—perceives/realizes; guṇebhyaḥ ca—and beyond the gunas; param—the Supreme Transcendence; vetti—knows; mat-bhāvam—My divine nature; saḥ—he; adhigacchati—attains.
verses.translation: When the awakened seer perceives no doer other than the three gunas, and knows That (the Supreme Self) which is transcendental to the gunas, he attains to My divine nature.
verses.meaning: Liberation occurs through double discernment: (1) Recognizing that all bodily actions, thoughts, and feelings are the gunas interacting with gunas, and (2) Realizing that the pure Atman is the non-doer witness beyond all gunas. This insight frees the seeker from all karmic entanglement.
verses.purport: Liberation occurs through double discernment: (1) Recognizing that all bodily actions, thoughts, and feelings are the gunas interacting with gunas, and (2) Realizing that the pure Atman is the non-doer witness beyond all gunas. This insight frees the seeker from all karmic entanglement.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
गुणानेतानतीत्य त्रीन्देही देहसमुद्भवान् |
जन्ममृत्युजरादुःखैर्विमुक्तोऽमृतमश्नुते || २० ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
गुणानेतानतीत्य त्रीन्देही देहसमुद्भवान् |
जन्ममृत्युजरादुःखैर्विमुक्तोऽमृतमश्नुते || २० ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
guṇānetānatītya trīndehī dehasamudbhavān |
janmamṛtyujarāduḥkhairvimukto'mṛtamaśnute || 20 ||
verses.word_meanings: guṇān—the gunas; etān—these; atītya—having transcended; trīn—three; dehī—the embodied soul; deha-samudbhavān—which give rise to the physical body; janma-mṛtyu-jarā-duḥkhaiḥ—from the miseries of birth, death, and old age; vimuktaḥ—liberated; amṛtam—immortality / divine nectar; aśnute—experiences/attains.
verses.translation: Having transcended these three gunas which originate in the material body, the embodied soul is freed from the miseries of birth, death, old age, and sorrow, and attains immortality.
verses.meaning: Transcendence of the Gunas is the very definition of Mukti (liberation). The soul ceases to identify with the biological vehicle and reclaims its birthright of eternal life and bliss.
verses.purport: Transcendence of the Gunas is the very definition of Mukti (liberation). The soul ceases to identify with the biological vehicle and reclaims its birthright of eternal life and bliss.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
कैर्लिङ्गैस्त्रीन्गुणानेतानतीतो भवति प्रभो |
किमाचारः कथं चैतांस्त्रीन्गुणानतिवर्तते || २१ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
कैर्लिङ्गैस्त्रीन्गुणानेतानतीतो भवति प्रभो |
किमाचारः कथं चैतांस्त्रीन्गुणानतिवर्तते || २१ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
kairliṅgaistrīnguṇānetānatīto bhavati prabho |
kimācāraḥ kathaṃ caitāṃstrīnguṇānativartate || 21 ||
verses.word_meanings: arjunaḥ uvāca—Arjuna said; kaiḥ liṅgaiḥ—by what characteristics/marks; trīn guṇān etān—these three gunas; atītaḥ—transcended; bhavati—is; prabho—O Lord; kim ācāraḥ—what is his conduct; katham—how; ca—and; etān trīn guṇān—these three modes; ativartate—does he transcend/cross over.
verses.translation: Arjuna said: By what marks is he recognized who has transcended these three gunas, O Lord? What is his conduct, and how does he cross beyond these three modes?
verses.meaning: Arjuna asks a three-part practical question reminiscent of the Sthitaprajna inquiry in Chapter 2: (1) What are the psychological marks of a Gunatita? (2) How does he live and act in the world? (3) By what method does one transcend the gunas?
verses.purport: Arjuna asks a three-part practical question reminiscent of the Sthitaprajna inquiry in Chapter 2: (1) What are the psychological marks of a Gunatita? (2) How does he live and act in the world? (3) By what method does one transcend the gunas?

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
प्रकाशं च प्रवृत्तिं च मोहमेव च पाण्डव |
न द्वेष्टि सम्प्रवृत्तानि न निवृत्तानि काङ्क्षति || २२ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
प्रकाशं च प्रवृत्तिं च मोहमेव च पाण्डव |
न द्वेष्टि सम्प्रवृत्तानि न निवृत्तानि काङ्क्षति || २२ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
prakāśaṃ ca pravṛttiṃ ca mohameva ca pāṇḍava |
na dveṣṭi sampravṛttāni na nivṛttāni kāṅkṣati || 22 ||
verses.word_meanings: śrī-bhagavān uvāca—the Supreme Lord said; prakāśam—illumination (Sattva); ca—and; pravṛttim—activity (Rajas); ca—and; moham—delusion (Tamas); eva ca—and also; pāṇḍava—O son of Pandu (Arjuna); na dveṣṭi—does not hate; sampravṛttāni—when they arise; na nivṛttāni—nor when they cease; kāṅkṣati—longs for.
verses.translation: The Supreme Lord said: O Pandava, he who does not hate illumination (Sattva), activity (Rajas), or delusion (Tamas) when they arise, nor longs for them when they cease;
verses.meaning: In Verses 22–25, Sri Krishna paints the portrait of the Gunatita. The liberated master does not react with aversion when gunas rise in the mind or body, nor does he crave them when they subside. He observes their coming and going with unshakeable inner serenity.
verses.purport: In Verses 22–25, Sri Krishna paints the portrait of the Gunatita. The liberated master does not react with aversion when gunas rise in the mind or body, nor does he crave them when they subside. He observes their coming and going with unshakeable inner serenity.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
उदासीनवदासीनो गुणैर्यो न विचाल्यते |
गुणा वर्तन्त इत्येवं योऽवतिष्ठति नेङ्गते || २३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
उदासीनवदासीनो गुणैर्यो न विचाल्यते |
गुणा वर्तन्त इत्येवं योऽवतिष्ठति नेङ्गते || २३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
udāsīnavadāsīno guṇairyo na vicālyate |
guṇā vartanta ityevaṃ yo'vatiṣṭhati neṅgate || 23 ||
verses.word_meanings: udāsīna-vat—like an unconcerned/neutral witness; āsīnaḥ—seated; guṇaiḥ—by the gunas; yaḥ—whoever; na vicālyate—is not agitated/shaken; guṇāḥ vartante—the gunas operate among the gunas; iti evam—knowing thus; yaḥ—who; avatiṣṭhati—remains established; na iṅgate—wavers not.
verses.translation: He who, seated like an unconcerned witness (Udasinavat), is not disturbed by the gunas, and knowing that 'the gunas alone are interacting with the gunas', remains steadfast and wavers not;
verses.meaning: The Gunatita adopts the stance of the detached witness (Sakshi/Udasina). Recognizing that sensory organs (gunas) are merely responding to external sense objects (gunas), he never identifies with the storm of transient emotions or bodily states.
verses.purport: The Gunatita adopts the stance of the detached witness (Sakshi/Udasina). Recognizing that sensory organs (gunas) are merely responding to external sense objects (gunas), he never identifies with the storm of transient emotions or bodily states.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
समदुःखसुखः स्वस्थः समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः |
तुल्यप्रियाप्रियो धीरस्तुल्यनिन्दात्मसंस्तुतिः || २४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
समदुःखसुखः स्वस्थः समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः |
तुल्यप्रियाप्रियो धीरस्तुल्यनिन्दात्मसंस्तुतिः || २४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
samaduḥkhasukhaḥ svasthaḥ samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanaḥ |
tulyapriyāpriyo dhīrastulyanindātmasaṃstutiḥ || 24 ||
verses.word_meanings: sama-duḥkha-sukhaḥ—equipoised in sorrow and joy; sva-sthaḥ—established in his own true Self; sama-loṣṭa-aśma-kāñcanaḥ—regarding a lump of earth, a stone, and gold as equal; tulya-priya-apriyaḥ—equal to the pleasant and unpleasant; dhīraḥ—wise and steadfast; tulya-nindā-ātma-saṃstutiḥ—equal in blame and self-praise.
verses.translation: He who is equal in sorrow and joy, established in the Self (Svastha), viewing a clod of earth, a stone, and gold as of equal value, constant amidst the pleasant and unpleasant, steadfast (Dhira), and identical in praise and blame;
verses.meaning: The Sanskrit word 'Svastha' (established in one's true Self) is the root of true spiritual and psychological health. Free from worldly value-projections, the Gunatita looks upon mud and gold with equal detachment, unshaken by flattery or condemnation.
verses.purport: The Sanskrit word 'Svastha' (established in one's true Self) is the root of true spiritual and psychological health. Free from worldly value-projections, the Gunatita looks upon mud and gold with equal detachment, unshaken by flattery or condemnation.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तुल्यामानापमानयोस्तुल्यो मित्रारिपक्षयोः |
सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी गुणातीतः स उच्यते || २५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तुल्यामानापमानयोस्तुल्यो मित्रारिपक्षयोः |
सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी गुणातीतः स उच्यते || २५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
tulyāmānāpamānayostulyo mitrāripakṣayoḥ |
sarvārambhaparityāgī guṇātītaḥ sa ucyate || 25 ||
verses.word_meanings: tulyā māna-apamānayoḥ—equal in honor and dishonor; tulyaḥ mitra-ari-pakṣayoḥ—equal toward the camps of friend and foe; sarva-ārambha-parityāgī—renouncer of all selfish ego-driven undertakings; guṇa-atītaḥ—transcender of the gunas; saḥ—he; ucyate—is called.
verses.translation: He who is equal in honor and dishonor, equal toward the factions of friend and foe, and who has renounced all ego-driven undertakings—he is declared to have transcended the gunas (Gunatita).
verses.meaning: 'Sarvarambha-parityagi' does not mean abandoning righteous duties, but renouncing the ego-sense of doership ('I am the master planner') and selfish ambition. Treating friends and adversaries with impartial compassion, such a soul rests in unalloyed peace.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मां च योऽव्यभिचारेण भक्तियोगेन सेवते |
स गुणान्समतीत्यैतान्ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते || २६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मां च योऽव्यभिचारेण भक्तियोगेन सेवते |
स गुणान्समतीत्यैतान्ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते || २६ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
māṃ ca yo'vyabhicāreṇa bhaktiyogena sevate |
sa guṇānsamatītyaitānbrahmabhūyāya kalpate || 26 ||
verses.word_meanings: mām—unto Me (the Supreme Lord); ca—and; yaḥ—whoever; avyabhicāreṇa—unswerving / unalloyed / unbroken; bhakti-yogena—by the yoga of devotion; sevate—serves; saḥ—he; guṇān—the gunas; samatītya—completely transcending; etān—these; brahma-bhūyāya—for realization of / absorption into Brahman; kalpate—becomes eligible/fit.
verses.translation: He who serves Me with unswerving, exclusive Bhakti Yoga transcends completely all these three gunas and becomes fit for realization of Brahman.
verses.meaning: Answering Arjuna's third question ('How does one transcend the gunas?'), Sri Krishna delivers the supreme secret: Unalloyed loving devotion (Avyabhicarini Bhakti) to the Supreme Lord. By surrendering to God, divine grace effortlessly burns through the gravitational pull of the three gunas, qualifying the devotee for Brahman realization.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ब्रह्मणो हि प्रतिष्ठाहममृतस्याव्ययस्य च |
शाश्वतस्य च धर्मस्य सुखस्यैकान्तिकस्य च || २७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ब्रह्मणो हि प्रतिष्ठाहममृतस्याव्ययस्य च |
शाश्वतस्य च धर्मस्य सुखस्यैकान्तिकस्य च || २७ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
brahmaṇo hi pratiṣṭhāhamamṛtasyāvyayasya ca |
śāśvatasya ca dharmasya sukhasyaikāntikasya ca || 27 ||
verses.word_meanings: brahmaṇaḥ—of the impersonal Brahman; hi—indeed; pratiṣṭhā—the basis / foundation / abode; aham—I (Sri Krishna); amṛtasya—of the immortal; avyayasya—of the immutable; ca—and; śāśvatasya—of the eternal; ca—and; dharmasya—of Dharma; sukhasya aikāntikasya—of absolute, unalloyed bliss; ca—and.
verses.translation: For I am the foundational basis and abode of the immortal and immutable Brahman, of eternal Dharma, and of unalloyed, infinite Bliss.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna concludes Chapter 14 with one of the most majestic declarations in Vedic literature: He is the ultimate foundation (Pratishtha) of the all-pervading Brahman, the eternal custodian of Dharma, and the infinite fountainhead of supreme transcendental Bliss (Aikantika Sukha). Surrender to Krishna is the direct attainment of all spiritual goals.
